footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $2.2M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 11.8% to $73.6M in 2025. Net interest income rose 11.1% to $69.5M and noninterest income rose 23.8% to $4.0M; noninterest expense fell 25.2%, and the provision for credit losses was −$70K, versus $6.8M.
Net income to common was $13.5M, versus −$12.1M, or $1.76 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 74.1% versus 110.8%. MainStreet Bancshares returned $7.4M through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common was $13.5M, versus −$12.1M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: MainStreet Bancshares, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
